summary: CPU-ONLY extension of the suffix gate for the user leg-grow design: the MTP head builds the cat10-shape caterpillar (spine + (n-1) legs/depth + root sibling) at width n=1..5, and suffix decoding GROWS THE LEGS (and tip) into multi-token chains. Measure where suffix grafts pay off most (shallow legs vs deep tip), model the leg-RESCUE (spine diverges -> leg catches -> leg suffix continues), sweep n=1..5, all under the ASYMMETRIC cost model (MTP depth costs MTP-head forwards, suffix growth is a FREE lookup; verify rows cost per-node). Output the best accept/event-per-cost config + what only the GPU arm can confirm. NO GPU.

data.costNumbers:
ASYMMETRIC COST MODEL — measured numbers to rank configs by accept/event PER COST:

PER-NODE VERIFY-ROW TAX (one extra tree node = one extra lm-head verify row; suffix-grown depth pays THIS but no head forward) — FR13_CAT10_BIND.md AXIS-3 (:80-86):
- cat9 (9 rows): 0.2258 s/fwd, warm 18.40 TPS, per-req median 16.01 TPS, 9 verify rows.
- cat10 (10 rows): 0.2287 s/fwd, warm 17.08 TPS, per-req median 15.17, 10 verify rows.
- native_e5 (5 rows): 0.2171 s/fwd, warm 10.78, per-req 9.72, 5 rows.
- MEASURED +1-row tax (cat10 vs cat9, B=1): +0.0029 s/fwd = ~2.9 ms/node ("1.013x", the +1 lm-head row). Stated +15 ms/row is an UPPER bound; B=1 actual ~2.9 ms/node. This is the per-VERIFY-ROW cost that suffix-grown legs/tail pay.

PER-FORWARD TAX SCALING WITH N (verify cost grows superlinearly above row-traffic floor) — FR13_SPEED_TAX_BASELINE.md THE TABLE (:31-36) + n=2 scaling (:50-60):
- native MTP-5 (N=5): 0.2127 s/fwd [M] = baseline. legacy chain5 (N=5): 0.3517. legacy cat9 (N=9): 0.3936-0.3976 (3 boots agree <1%). replay cat9 (N=9): 0.3270.
- OLS fit (:55, FIT not measurement, 2 distinct N): slope 0.0108 s/fwd per draft node, intercept 0.298 s. Measured step N=5->9 = +42-46 ms/fwd ~= 7x the row-traffic floor (+6.3 ms predicted) -> the per-node verify cost is dominated by tree graph/scheduler path, not lm-head rows alone.
- Replay route per-node GDN traffic ~2.9 ms/node (FR13_CAT10_BIND axis-3 framing); replay compute FREE (<1% of 99 ms weight-BW floor, 27GB/273GB/s) per FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS.md:68.

MTP-HEAD-FORWARD COST (MTP DEPTH = sequential head passes; the cost suffix-grown depth AVOIDS): native MTP-5 = 5 sequential head passes to draft depth-5 (fr10_mtp_draft_trace shape [1,5] = 5 head outputs/event). The task's cost model is correct and substantiated: MTP-grown depth d costs d head forwards; MTP WIDTH (top-k at an existing depth) is free (topk of that depth's logits); SUFFIX-grown depth costs only verify rows (~2.9 ms/node) + GDN node traffic, NO head forward => suffix-grown depth is STRICTLY cheaper than MTP-grown depth, exactly per the asymmetric model. Per-forward s/fwd numbers above are sum-basis ratios valid WITHIN matched-shape table only (not absolute latency) — class-12 rule, never multiply s/fwd x accept into a TPS.

measure.summary:
ANSWER TO THE OPEN QUESTION: growing the LEGS does NOT beat growing the TIP, under both the exact per-graft payoff and the modeled rescue. Reason: suffix continuation payoff is FLAT across graft depth (E[min CL,3] ~1.43-1.70 everywhere), so the leg's only advantage would be catching divergences the tip misses — but the modeled leg-rescue sums to just ~1.08 tokens (tail3), and that depends on the LEAST-reliable capped d0 catch (0.95, raw 1.76 = the cat9-vs-native trajectory confound, NOT a real rank-2 recovery). At matched MTP-head forwards, growing the TIP wins at every extra-node budget (TIP A/E 2.33->2.94 vs LEGS 2.17->2.55).

WHY: the asymmetric cost model makes suffix-grown depth strictly cheaper than MTP depth, so the cost-optimal config is minimal-spine + a suffix TIP tail (the prior baseline). Legs cost the same verify rows but their modeled rescue yield is lower than just extending the main line, because the tip is reached by the surviving spine mass which is large early (cat9 d0/d1 accept 0.871/0.828) and the suffix continuation from the tip is as long as from any leg.

BEST CONFIG: n=1 is the most cost-efficient (A/cost 0.450); the raw-accept peak is n=2 (A/E 3.43, spineD3 + 3 legs + tip4, 14 nodes) but it (a) barely beats tip-only and (b) leans on the modeled/approx leg numbers. The tip-grow baseline to beat (E[min CL,3]=2.32 leaky / 1.90 strict) stands; legs add at most ~+0.4 A/E in the optimistic modeled case and lose under cost.

CAVEAT: the decisive leg-RESCUE numbers are MODELED because no per-depth MTP top-k drafts exist on CPU (confirmed across all banked captures). A GPU run exposing per-depth top-k logprobs would be needed to confirm/refute the leg-catch rates (especially the unreliable d0). This is the cheap CPU pre-screen only; the screen says TIP >= LEGS, so prioritize the tip-grow build. Recommend NOT investing in the leg-grow GPU prototype until/unless the d0 catch rate is measured directly.

redteam.noLeakage: PASS. The leakage guard is carried over verbatim from the prior gate's suffix_replay.py (only a comment string differs; all guard CODE is identical). Per-request structure is strictly causal: at position t the structure indexes only contexts ending before the predicted future, with assert len(history)==len(prompt)+t+1; build_global skips the target index (never self-indexes); pick_draft/greedy_continuation select by longest matching CONTEXT only, never peeking at the future. Three adversarial corruption probes I ran all collapse to EXACTLY 0.0: (a) built-in self-test base 2.2222 -> corrupted 0.0; (b) all-ladder-streams futures randomized -> PART1 ALL E[min CL,3] 1.5413 -> 0.0; (c) the deployment-realistic vector (corrupt ONLY target0's future, keep a CLEAN cross-request global corpus) -> 2.2222 -> 0.0, proving the target cannot predict its own future even with a clean global. No future-token leakage in either the EXACT PART1 measure or the global corpus.
redteam.rescueNotDoubleCounted: PASS, with one conservative-direction modeling flaw. The leg fires ONLY on the spine-reject mass: expected_rescued = p_diverge(=1-cat9_accept[d]) * p_catch * (1+E_suffix), and spine_accept_expected counts only survival/accept mass, so the leg's reject mass is disjoint from the spine's accept mass at each depth -> no overlap, correctly conditioned on spine-reject. FLAW (does not break the verdict): the model uses the CONDITIONAL reject rate 1-accept[d] without multiplying by the REACH probability (survival to depth d). This OVERSTATES leg rescue at deeper depths (e.g. d3 uses 0.517 but unconditional reach-weighted diverge is only 0.238). Reach-correcting reduces the tail3 leg-rescue sum from 1.0822 to ~0.7568. Crucially this bias is IN FAVOR OF LEGS (the losing arm), so correcting it only strengthens 'TIP beats LEGS'. The conclusion is conservative w.r.t. this flaw.
redteam.modeledFlaggedHonestly: PASS. EXACT (suffix continuation payoff by graft depth in PART1; tip suffix accepts in PART3) and MODELED (leg-catch via banked cat9 reject x greedy deficits) are cleanly separated and labeled per-n (EXACT / MODELED top-2 / APPROX top-k>2 geometric). The decisive 'legs lose' verdict does NOT depend on the n>2 geometric APPROX: (a) the accept-per-cost optimizer never selects any leg at ANY n (all cost-optimal configs are tip-only, legDepths=0), and (b) the direct matched-budget leg-vs-tip comparison uses n=2 top-2 only (the modeled-but-not-approximated catch). The single native-beating number (raw-accept 3.43) is correctly stated as NOT claimable on CPU because it lives entirely inside the modeled leg rescue, ~63% of which is the explicitly-flagged least-reliable capped d0 catch (raw 1.76 = the cat9-vs-native trajectory confound, not a real rank-2 recovery).
redteam.costModelCorrect: PASS. cost = N_nodes*PER_NODE_TAX + spine_depth*MTP_HEAD_COST, where head forwards = the MTP-DRAFTED spine depth ONLY. Verified directly: spineD1+tip3+rootsib (5 nodes) costs 6.0 = 5 verify nodes + 1 head forward (NOT 1+3); suffix tip/leg growth adds verify rows at zero head-forward cost. The asymmetry holds: a suffix-grown depth-4 line (cost ~5) is strictly cheaper than an all-MTP depth-4 spine (cost 8 = 4 nodes + 4 head forwards). This correctly makes the optimizer minimize head forwards -> minimal spine + suffix tip tail.
redteam.legsBeatTipTrustworthy: FALSE is TRUSTWORTHY and survives the thin corpus + modeled rescue. Three independent lines, the load-bearing ones EXACT: (1) EXACT suffix payoff is essentially FLAT across graft depth (E[min CL,3] ~1.43-1.70 at d0..d5), so a leg has no intrinsic payoff edge over the tip; (2) TIP wins ALL 8 matched-MTP-head-forward budgets in the direct comparison (n=2 top-2 modeled, NO geometric approx); (3) legs never enter the cost-optimal set at any n. The only number that nominally beats native (3.43) is entirely inside the modeled leg rescue (EXACT tip-only arm is 2.94, below native 3.16), and the reach-omission flaw biases toward legs, so correcting it widens the tip's margin. Thin corpus (4 astropy tasks, 508 step-aligned + 4032 depth-agnostic positions) is a real limitation but the modeled legs would have to beat a FLAT exact payoff at a HIGHER reach-corrected catch rate to flip it.
redteam.gpuArmNext: The single decisive thing the GPU arm must measure is the TRUE per-depth leg-catch rate from REAL MTP head per-depth top-k drafts, ESPECIALLY the d0 catch. On CPU this is the only number that could flip the raw-accept verdict: it is currently capped at 0.95 (raw 1.76 = the cat9-vs-native trajectory confound), contributes ~63% of the modeled rescue, and the leg token IDENTITIES are fundamentally unknowable on CPU (confirmed: fr10_mtp_draft_trace.jsonl holds only the width-1 MTP-5 spine draft, no top-k alternates exist in any cat9/cat10/native capture). Secondary: re-derive leg rescue with REACH-weighting (multiply 1-accept[d] by survival-to-d) since the current model omits it. If the true reach-weighted d0 catch is low, legs lose by even more than the CPU pre-screen shows.
